root_cause.text: The s390 AP bus kept its own `struct ap_device::driver_override` pointer and accessed it from `ap_bus_revise_bindings()`/`__ap_revise_reserved()` and `ap_device_probe()` without the driver-core’s override lock, so a concurrent `driver_override_store()` could free the string and trigger a use-after-free race.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says `ap_bus_revise_bindings()` is called after `ap_attr_mutex` is released, and `__ap_revise_reserved()` “accesses the driver_override field without holding any lock, racing against a concurrent driver_override_store() that may free the old string”; the patch removes `struct ap_device::driver_override`, replaces raw checks with `device_match_driver_override()`/`device_has_driver_override()`, and changes sysfs access to `dev->driver_override.name` under `dev->driver_override.lock` via the generic driver-core infrastructure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the core driver-override matching helper when revising reserved AP queue devices so reprobe behavior follows the correct override semantics.
intent_record.what: The function __ap_revise_reserved() was changed to declare a new local variable ovrd and, for queue devices, replace direct inspection of ap_dev->driver_override and strcmp() against ap_drv->driver.name with a call to device_match_driver_override(dev, &ap_drv->driver). The old ap_dev pointer declaration was removed. The new logic handles three cases: ovrd > 0 does nothing, ovrd == 0 triggers reprobe, and negative values fall through to the existing mutex-protected path.
intent_record.how: Runtime behavior now relies on the kernel's driver-override matching helper instead of manually comparing the override string to the driver name. This makes the decision to reprobe or skip reprobe follow the standard device-core matching semantics, avoiding duplicated logic and ensuring the queue is reprobed only when the override does not match the bound driver.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the device core helper to correctly detect driver overrides when determining AP default-driver ownership.
intent_record.what: In `ap_owned_by_def_drv(int card, int queue)`, the `override` boolean assignment changed from directly checking `!!aq->ap_dev.driver_override` to calling `device_has_driver_override(&aq->ap_dev.device)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now determines whether a driver override is present using the device core’s helper instead of a direct field test, which aligns the ownership check with the device model’s canonical override state and may account for internal representation changes or additional override handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new local variable for upcoming probe logic in `ap_device_probe()`.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration in `ap_device_probe()` was extended by adding a new integer variable `ovrd` to the existing declaration list, while leaving the initial value of `rc` as `-ENODEV` unchanged.
intent_record.how: This change only affects the function's available local state at runtime by reserving storage for `ovrd`; it does not alter control flow or behavior by itself, but likely supports additional probe logic introduced elsewhere in the function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch AP device probing to the standard driver-override matching helper so override handling follows kernel core semantics.
intent_record.what: In `ap_device_probe()`, the manual `ap_dev->driver_override` string comparison was replaced with a call to `device_match_driver_override(dev, &ap_drv->driver)`. The result is stored in `ovrd`, and the probe now explicitly handles three cases: `ovrd > 0` as a successful override match, `ovrd == 0` as a mismatch that jumps to `out`, and the remaining case falling through to the existing permission-check logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, driver binding for AP devices now uses the kernel's standard override-matching helper instead of open-coded string comparison. This preserves the existing behavior of rejecting non-matching overrides while aligning probe selection with the device core's override semantics, including any special handling implemented by the helper.

intent_record.what: The `struct ap_device` definition no longer contains the `const char *driver_override;` member; all other shown fields remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: This removes per-device storage for a driver override string from AP devices, so code can no longer read or set that field through `struct ap_device` and any behavior depending on it is eliminated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the driver_override spinlock and direct device override field access in driver_override_show() instead of the generic device lock.
intent_record.what: In driver_override_show(), the code no longer casts the device to struct ap_queue, no longer accesses ap_dev->driver_override under device_lock()/device_unlock(), and instead acquires dev->driver_override.lock with guard(spinlock) before returning sysfs_emit(buf, "%s\n", dev->driver_override.name ?: ""). The variable declarations for aq, ap_dev, and rc were removed from this function, while driver_override_store() begins by removing the now-unused aq/ap_dev declarations.
intent_record.how: The show path now reads the device override name directly from the device's driver_override field while holding its dedicated spinlock, which avoids using the broader device lock and simplifies synchronized access to the override string. Runtime behavior remains to print the override value or an empty line when unset, but with protection aligned to the driver_override data structure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch driver override handling to the device core helpers so the override counter is updated from the real device override state.
intent_record.what: In driver_override_store(), the code now uses device_has_driver_override(dev) instead of checking ap_dev->driver_override directly, and it replaces driver_set_override(dev, &ap_dev->driver_override, buf, count) with __device_set_driver_override(dev, buf, count). The subsequent counter updates also now test device_has_driver_override(dev) rather than ap_dev->driver_override.
intent_record.how: The function now relies on the device core's override helpers to determine and update override state, which makes the counter bookkeeping follow the authoritative driver-override state managed by the device layer. This avoids depending on the AP device's local pointer field directly and ensures the override count is adjusted based on the actual post-call override presence.

This is the same area as the use-after-free root cause.
The change only adds a local variable in ap_device_probe() for upcoming probe logic and does not address the driver_override lifetime/race issue or the missing override lock.

The vulnerability is caused by unsafe access to the AP bus's own struct ap_device::driver_override pointer. Removing that field directly addresses the root cause by eliminating the buggy per-device override storage that could be raced and freed.

The change is about using the driver_override spinlock and direct field access in driver_override_show(), which affects how the override is read for display. The root cause is a use-after-free race in the s390 AP bus caused by accessing ap_device::driver_override without the driver-core override lock in binding/probe paths. This hunk does not address those AP bus code paths or the race condition described.

Author: Harald Freudenberger <freude@linux.ibm.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 19 16:27:36 2025 +0100

    s390/ap: Support driver_override for AP queue devices
    
    Add a new sysfs attribute driver_override the AP queue's
    directory. Writing in a string overrides the default driver
    determination and the drivers are matched against this string
    instead. This overrules the driver binding determined by the
    apmask/aqmask bitmask fields.

In `__ap_revise_reserved()` and `ap_device_probe()`, the code now checks `ap_dev->driver_override` and compares it with `ap_drv->driver.name` using `strcmp(...)`, otherwise it falls back to the apmask/aqmask logic. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause was the AP bus accessing its own `struct ap_device::driver_override` without the driver-core override lock, but this snippet is about introducing support for `driver_override` and does not show a separate unsafe custom override management path; instead it uses the existing device field directly in the normal driver_override logic. Because the diff does not show the old buggy custom string ownership/freeing or any additional unsafe AP-bus-managed override pointer, the vulnerable construct is absent here, and the code is already adjusted to honor `driver_override` in the probe/revise paths.
